name: LP 890-9 c
significanceText: Second only to the TRAPPIST-1 worlds as a place to search for an atmosphere — and a natural experiment in why Earth kept its oceans while Venus lost hers.
hostStar: LP 890-9 / SPECULOOS-2 (M6V ultracool dwarf, second-coolest known planet-hosting star after TRAPPIST-1)

name: TIC 52059926 b
significanceText: Barely made it into NASA's catalog before this list was written — still fresh, with astronomers just getting started on it.

name: TOI-2257 b
significanceText: Sits in the habitable zone on paper, but its wildly lopsided orbit swings the temperature from -80°C to 100°C over a single year — so much for comfortable.

name: TOI-715 b
significanceText: A nearby super-Earth sitting right in its star's habitable zone, close enough and bright enough that JWST can get a good look.

name: TOI-7166 b
significanceText: A temperate mini-Neptune confirmed in late 2025, already one of the best bets around for JWST to study up close.
